criteria.given: Eligible ordinary hash references include distinct values and deliberate same-prefix collisions in declared work scopes
then: The default minimum is six hexadecimal characters; valid per-work overrides are applied and invalid configuration is rejected
Only colliding references grow until unique in the declared scope; ambiguous inputs are rejected and never silently rebound
Operations requiring exact Git identity receive the resolved full object ID; prefixes supply no integrity authority
criteria.when: The system renders and resolves references with default and per-work minimum lengths

criteria.given: Tasks and tests include new numeric local IDs and legacy identifiers in multiple workstreams
then: New references use unpadded local IDs and readable work/task/task-id or work/test/task-id/test-id forms
Inherited work context is explicit and cross-workstream references identify their owner
Legacy mappings remain stable; published identifiers are neither recycled nor rebound
criteria.when: References are created, displayed, persisted, and resolved

criteria.given: Workflow records repeat contract, policy, source, review, or output digests under known digest semantics
then: A workstream catalog stores each full digest once per algorithm and digest semantics, and immutable revisions can reuse its entry
Downstream records use resolvable references and shared context rather than repeated full digests and metadata
Unique output digests remain authoritative full values and edited outputs invalidate their evidence
criteria.when: New-format records are registered and downstream reports are generated

criteria.given: A coordinator has accepted exact contract obligations and a candidate can edit its own JSON files and aliases
then: Resolution remains anchored to coordinator-owned accepted-tests authority and registered review/run records
Candidate-only modifications cannot authorize changed obligations or independent decisions
The existing exact intent approval and attributable independent review requirements remain enforced
criteria.when: The candidate replaces a manifest, changes a referenced contract, or claims independent approval

criteria.given: An accepted contract revision has historical evidence and a later run produces new logs
then: Adding run evidence leaves published contract entries unchanged
Contract pins and run/evidence records have separate immutable lifetimes
Historical references retain their original meaning; evidence for stale obligations cannot satisfy a different accepted contract
criteria.when: New contract and evidence records are registered and old references are reloaded

criteria.given: Canonical-JSON contracts and byte-bound intent/log artifacts have registered checksum semantics
then: Contract comparisons preserve the existing canonical sorted compact JSON equivalence rules
Intent confirmation and log verification preserve exact-byte invalidation
Full algorithm and digest semantics are resolved for each checksum; display prefixes and different semantics cannot be substituted
criteria.when: JSON whitespace or key order changes, or exact artifact bytes change

criteria.given: A record derives tracked content from a full pinned Git commit and repository-relative path
then: Validation reads the exact pinned object and applies its required byte or canonical-JSON semantics
Unavailable commits or paths and unsafe paths fail explicitly without falling back to HEAD or current worktree bytes
Uncommitted output logs retain a registered full digest and available artifact
criteria.when: Validation resolves its content with present, absent, changed, or unsafe targets

criteria.given: Workstreams and branches have overlapping local numbers, stale concurrent registrations, malformed references, and cyclic targets
then: References resolve by sufficient work, record-type, and immutable target context
Registration serializes updates and rejects stale conflicting publication or allocates a fresh identity before publication
Existing identities remain unchanged and missing, ambiguous, cyclic, or malformed references fail with a stable scoped reason
criteria.when: The coordinator registers or resolves records

criteria.given: Equivalent workflow data includes absent, null, empty, Unicode, and repeated shared-context values
then: Generated workflow JSON uses compact versioned serialization with shared context recorded once per group
Values and required evidence survive normalization; only schema-declared defaults permit field omission
Canonical validation is deterministic and absent, null, and empty remain distinguishable where required
criteria.when: New writers serialize it and supported readers normalize and validate it

criteria.given: Legacy and new records contain actual approvals, executions, Git dependencies, and provenance
then: Supported legacy records remain readable without rewriting history
Migration preserves originals and provenance without inventing approval, execution, or Red/Green history
Export includes required immutable records and Git objects, or reports missing dependencies and refuses verified completeness
Unsupported versions and incomplete imports fail with explicit migration or availability reasons
criteria.when: Records are read, explicitly migrated, exported, and reloaded

criteria.given: An agent needs status, one task/test, or selected review/execution evidence from a large workstream
then: The projection supplies sufficient declared reference context and retrieves requested evidence on demand
The complete integrity catalog is not loaded by default
Failure output identifies unresolved references and scope; detailed evidence remains retrievable
criteria.when: The agent requests a compact projection and follows references needed for its task

criteria.given: Before implementation a corpus, source baseline, tokenizer identity/version, and deterministic equivalent workloads are frozen as specified in the Markdown proposal
then: Token totals include all necessary agent inputs and reference lookup responses; metadata byte totals include shared catalogs
All required evidence and equivalent questions are retained, using representative real workflow artifacts as well as collision fixtures
Aggregate input tokens and generated metadata JSON bytes are both strictly lower than baseline
The report records exact baseline/candidate identities, workload and tokenizer versions, per-journey totals, aggregate totals, individual regressions, and retained full-value exceptions
criteria.when: Baseline and new resume, independent-review, and completion journeys are measured with the same tokenizer

criteria.given: A record publication or coordinator registration is interrupted and then retried
then: Readers observe complete old or complete new published state and never a successful dangling reference
Retries preserve existing immutable targets and reject conflicting stale state
Fixture locks, processes, runtime files, and worktrees are cleaned without leaving real source changes uncommitted
criteria.when: Readers load the registry and the coordinator recovers the operation

criteria.given: An isolated end-to-end workflow accepts contracts, executes tests, registers independent review, and retains source/log/runner identities
then: Valid evidence retains the existing completion outcome and exact source/candidate/contract lineage
Changed logs, stale obligations, substituted manifests, missing objects, and invalid review or execution evidence refuse completion
Readable IDs, reference resolution, legacy access, and export/reload work through actual workflow entry points
criteria.when: It queries compact records and checks final completion with valid and deliberately altered evidence

criteria.given: Derived artifact revisions have declared actual dependencies, including spec-to-plan, plan-to-task, task-to-test, and other existing source, policy, runner, review, or evidence relationships
then: Every derived revision retains immutable identities for all actual inputs; its canonical checksum covers content and complete work/type/revision-qualified input bindings
Changing, adding, or removing an input binding requires regeneration or explicit revalidation and a new immutable derived revision and checksum even if the substantive payload is unchanged
Review and coordinator acceptance follow existing requirements for each artifact type; digest, alias, catalog, or pointer edits alone cannot establish derivation or transfer approval
Historical artifact and execution bindings remain unchanged; historical runs cannot be relabeled as new executions and reuse must satisfy existing evidence eligibility rules
The dependency inventory covers every actual relationship without inferring a dependency merely from ownership or an ordinary lookup link
Canonical-equivalent formatting changes preserve existing equivalence rules without artificial semantic revisions
criteria.when: An input revision or a derived artifact input binding changes and the new workflow context tries to consume existing artifacts

criteria.given: A declared dependency graph contains a multi-level chain, shared and multiple-input descendants, an unrelated branch, and retained historical revisions
then: All directly and transitively affected descendants are identified as stale for the new context, even before intermediate artifacts or their checksums are rewritten
A multiple-input artifact remains ineligible while any required binding is stale, missing, or invalid
Affected artifacts are regenerated or explicitly revalidated in dependency order with new bindings, revisions, checksums, and required review/acceptance before becoming eligible
Unrelated branches and upstream artifacts are not unnecessarily revised; historical contexts continue to resolve their original exact graph
Existing cycle, missing-reference, and conflicting-identity rejection still applies while traversing dependencies
criteria.when: A root or intermediate input changes semantically in the selected current workflow context
